1.

The present claim arises out of a detailed accident report (DAR), filed by the police in terms of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act and the same is treated as a claim petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act.
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 08.04.2017 injured Mukesh Kumar was returning home on his motorcycle bearing no.HR-51H-1506.
At around 12.20 am, when he reached near MB Road T-point Okhla mod, one vehicle coming from Badarpur side at a high speed,driven in a rash and negligent manner hit his motorcycle.
He sustained injuries on his right leg and hand.
He was taken to AIIMS hospital for treatment.
3. An FIR no.72/2017 dated 09.04.2017 was registered u/s 279, 337 IPC.
Matter was investigated and statement of injured was recorded.
During investigation, one Subhash Das met the IO and stated that on 08.04.2017 at about 12.30 am, he was going towards Lal Kuan after closing his shop.

When he reached T- point of Okhla, he saw the injured lying on the road alongwith his motorcycle and a Hydra Crane no.DL1M-4534 (hereinafter referred to as offending Crane) alongwith his driver was found standing/parked there.
Thereafter, boy came in a car and took the injured to the hospital in his car.
The informant provided the number of Hydra Crane to the police and left the spot.

4 . sentences.text: 5. Respondent no.1 is the driver and Respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending Crane.
The offending Crane was not insured on the date of accident.
6. Respondent no.1 and 2 filed their reply denying the involvement of offending Crane and refuting their liability.

7. Vide order dated 23.12.2017, following issues were framed.
1.

Whether the injured Sh. Mukesh Kumar suffered injuries in a road traffic accident dated 08.04.2017 involving vehicle bearing no.DL-1M-4534 driven by R1 and owned by R2 and not insured, due to rash and negligent driving of R1?

OPP. 
2. Whether the claimant is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP. 
3. Relief.
8.

He deposed on the lines of DAR and stated that he was working in private company at Gurgaon and was earning Rs.50,900/-.
He sustained a disability of 16% in relation to right lower limb & right upper limb.
He deposed that he was admitted in the hospital on 08.04.2017 and discharged on 09.04.2017.
He took treatment as outpatient and could not move without help.

His right leg remained plastered even Mukesh Kumar (Dar) vs Sarwan Khan (72/17 Pp Pur) on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111462724/

He relied upon documents i.e. election card as Ex.PW-1/1, DL,RC insurance policy of his motorcycle as Ex.PW-1/2 to Ex.PW-1/4, DAR as Ex.PW-1/5, disability certificate as Ex.PW-1/6, original medical bills as Ex.PW-1/7 to Ex.PW-1/22, original treatment record as Ex.PW-1/23 and Ex.PW-1/40 and salary slip as Ex.PW-1/41.
He was duly cross- examined learned counsel for Respondent no.1 and 2.
Sh. Neeraj was examined as PW-2.
He relied upon copy of payslip of injured for March 2017 as Ex.PW-2/1.
He was not cross-examined by Respondent no.1 and 2 despite opportunity.
No evidence has been led on behalf of the respondents.
9. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of both the parties.
On the basis of pleadings of the parties, evidence adduced and arguments addressed, issue wise findings are as under:

Whether the injured Sh. Mukesh Kumar suffered injuries in a road traffic accident dated 08.04.2017 involving vehicle bearing no.DL-1M-4534 driven by R1 and owned by R2 and not insured due to rash and negligent driving of R1? OPP.
10.

Before proceeding to decide the above issue, it is apposite to note that as a settled principle of law, proceedings under The Motor Vehicle Act are not considered akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not applicable.
MACT NO 621/17 Mukesh Kumar v. Sarvar Khan P.No. 4 Of 9 BK Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs.
Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken.

sentences.text: 11. In the instant case, petitioner Mukesh Kumar has testified the date as well as the manner of accident.

Since respondents have denied the involvement of the offending vehicle, the chargesheet,
which forms a part of the DAR and relied upon by the petitioner as Ex.PW-1/5, has been carefully perused.
As per the chargesheet,IO SI Umrao Singh received information about an accident through PCR call.
The time he reached the spot and till he took photographs of the spot, no eye witness was found.
Subsequently, he received information that the injured was admitted in the hospital.

At the hospital, IO recorded statement of the injured who stated "...main mukesh kumar s/o Nek Sahai ......tatha Gurgaon, Haryana me private service karta hun, tatha deenak 08.04.2017 ki raat ghar ko lautate hue 12.20 baje raatri apni motorcycle no.HR-51AH-1506 Hero Honda Splender Plus Mukesh Kumar (Dar) vs Sarwan Khan (72/17 Pp Pur) on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111462724/

Tatha motorcycle bhi damage ho gayi.
Accident karne wali gaadi ka chaalak apni gaadi lekar mauke se bhaag gaya.
Police ki gaadi me mujhe AIIMS Trauma Center, New Delhi baraye illaz daakhil karaya.
Naamalum gaadi ke chalak ke khilaf kanooni karwai ki jaaye..."
Even during his cross-examination, PW-1 has categorically admitted that he could not see the registration number of the offending vehicle at the time of accident as he had got unconscious.
On the contrary, there is nothing in the MLC to show that the injured was brought in an unconscious state or that he was unfit to make a statement before the police at that time.

In fact, as per the statement of the injured recorded by the police soon after the accident, he has categorically stated that it was "gaadi" (car) with unknown number that had hit him and that such car fled from the spot after the accident.

The version recorded by the police is clearly contradictory not only with the version of petitioner in the claim petition but also with the statement of one Subhash recorded by the police who informed that when he reached the spot, he saw the injured and his motorcycle lying on the road and one Crane Hydra was also standing there.
In his cross-examination, PW-1 specifically stated that it was the IO/police official who informed him the registration number of the offending vehicle.

In the same statement, he also testified that he did not remember after how many days he was informed about the number of the offending MACT NO 621/17 Mukesh Kumar v. Sarvar Khan P.No. 6 Of 9 BK vehicle.
As per the informant of the accident namely Subhash, it was some boy who had taken the injured in his car to the hospital.
It was after the injured was taken to the hospital that the police arrived at the spot and recorded statement of such person namely Subhash.
As such, even the version of the IO that he had not found any witness on the spot is discrepant with the version of recording statement of Subhash.
Since as per the chargesheet it is only Subhash who had seen the offending Crane standing at the spot, his evidence was crucial to be recorded in the present case.
Petitioner has conveniently not examined any witness apart from himself.

The presence of the offending crane on the spot becomes even more doubtful due to the fact that despite the investigating officer and alleged witness Subhash claiming the offending Crane to have remained at the spot, no photographs of such Crane were taken at the time when the photographs of motorcycle of the injured were clicked.
The seizure of the offending crane is reflected to be four days after the accident and thus there is an obvious delay in obtaining mechanical inspection report of such Crane.

The presence of Crane on the spot is also ruled out by the statement of the injured wherein he has stated that the offending vehicle had already fled from the spot by the time he was taken to the hospital.

Further, there is contradiction in the version of claimant and that of one Mukesh Kumar (Dar) vs Sarwan Khan (72/17 Pp Pur) on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111462724/
4 Subhash, in the fact that the injured has claimed in his statement before the police that he was taken to AIIMS Trauma Center in the PCR/police vehicle while as per alleged independent witness it was some boy who MACT NO 621/17 Mukesh Kumar v. Sarvar Khan P.No. 7 Of 9 BK had taken the injured in his car.

sentences.text: In fact, the MLC also reflects the name of the person who brought the victim to hospital as Murari Lal also mentioned in list of witnesses(annexed with chargesheet) as HC Murari Lal.

The involvement of the offending Crane further become suspicious from the fact that the petitioner has throughout claimed that the offending vehicle had been at a very high speed, while it is a matter of common knowledge that a Crane of the model and design claimed to be involved in the accident,
can, at maximum, be driven at a speed of 29 Km/h.
In his cross- examination also, PW-1 has failed to specify the speed of offending vehicle even on an approximate basis.
Further, the mechanical inspection report of the Crane shows front bumper dent and crack on the left and right side of the windows.
The manner of accident described by the petitioner is unlikely to cause damage to the front "bumper" of the Crane and both the windows of such Crane, at the same time.

The fact that a Crane is a huge vehicle where even the distance of its front portion from its windows is remote and far from its booms & hooks, the damage revealed in the report does not appear to have a nexus with the accident.
Due to its unique structure, it is highly unlikely that even a layman would ever describe a Crane to be a "gaadi".

As such, not only the fact that no eye witness who could have identified the offending vehicle causing the accident has been examined but also due to the reason that the victim himself has admitted that he had not noted the number of the offending vehicle and has given contradictory version qua involvement of a high speed gaadi or a Crane, involvement of the offending Crane MACT NO 621/17 Mukesh Kumar v. Sarvar Khan P.No. 8 Of 9 BK is seriously under doubt.

sentences.text:
As such,
it is held that the petitioner has failed to even bleakly prove by preponderance of probabilities that the accident was caused with the involvement of the offending vehicle/crane.
Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of respondents and against the petitioner.
Issue no. 2
Whether the claimant is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP. 
12.
In view of the discussion in issue no.1, issue no. 2 is accordingly decided.

However, since it is not disputed that the petitioner suffered injury on account of a road accident and there is possibility that the same may have been caused by an unknown vehicle, petitioner is at liberty to approach concerned DLSA for relief of compensation, if any, if not already availed, under Section 396(4) of BNSS, as per which:
"Where the offender is not traced or identified, but the victim is identified, and where no trial takes place, the victim or his dependents may make an application to the State or the District Legal Services Authority for award of compensation".
13. Petition is accordingly dismissed.
